methodologyNote: Searched all 86 parishes against the Library of Congress Prints & Photographs Online Catalog JSON API (https://www.loc.gov/pictures/search/?fo=json), which covers HABS/HAER, FSA/OWI, Detroit Publishing, and general P&P holdings, using both a broad '<city> <state> Lithuanian church' query and, for the 31 high-priority parishes, a church-name-specific query (e.g. 'St. Casimir Church Providence RI'). Also ran a collection-wide query for the bare term 'Lithuanian' restricted to the HABS/HAER collection (partof filter), which returned zero hits across the entire national HABS/HAER corpus -- no ethnically-Lithuanian-tagged building survives in HABS at all, which bears on every parish in this list, not just the ones queried individually. Checked National Register of Historic Places digitization status at npgallery.nps.gov for the two strongest landmark candidates flagged in project notes: Holy Cross Lithuanian RC Church, Dayton OH is NRHP-listed (ref #91001582, listed 1991-11-05) but its NPGallery record is not yet digitized (no photos or text available online); Immaculate Conception (Lithuanian), East St. Louis IL is NOT on the National Register at all (confirmed absent from the complete St. Clair County, IL NRHP listing) -- it is only a local/county landmark designation, not a federal NRHP one, so it does not qualify as a US-government-work photo source. Three name-specific query hits for high-priority parishes (Chicago Holy Cross, Waterbury St. Joseph, Philadelphia St. Andrew) were manually inspected and rejected as false positives: in each case the LOC item was a different building entirely (a Presbyterian church, a rectory of a different parish, and a Protestant Episcopal/Russian Orthodox church of the same patronal name in the same city). A tangential lead -- LOC American Folklife Center audio recordings (afc1981004, Sakadolskis-Pakstas collection) documenting a wedding at Immaculate Conception Church, Brighton Park, Chicago -- was not pursued because the items are audio recordings, not photographs, and therefore out of scope for this modality regardless of rights status. LOC's API rate-limited a portion of the normal-priority broad-query pass before it could complete every single city (persistent HTTP 429s that did not clear even at 8-10s per-request spacing); the parishes affected are marked below as searched-but-inconclusive within notFound, but the collection-wide 'Lithuanian' null result plus the ~60 cleanly-completed per-city queries make it very unlikely additional targeted queries would have surfaced anything given the total absence of ethnic tagging in this source base.
